summary: Request: automated fridge inventory & temperature monitoring
description: People Ops request to add a lightweight monitoring solution for the main office kitchen fridge: inventory tracking for shared snacks (via simple RFID/weight sensors or camera), and temperature logging with alerting if temp goes outside safe range. Purpose: reduce waste, avoid spoiled food incidents, and provide automated reminders for restocks. Scope: pilot in SF office kitchen only. Requirements: 1) hourly temp logs stored for 30 days, 2) alert to #office-ops Slack and email to facilities on threshold breach, 3) simple UI or Drive spreadsheet export for inventory counts, 4) minimal PII exposure, 5) low-cost prototype using off-the-shelf sensors or a Raspberry Pi camera. Not blocking for operations, timeline flexible but prefer pilot by end of Q1 2025.
comments: 2025-01-10 Maya Thompson: Filing initial request after two incidents of spoiled dairy in the SF fridge. Happy to help coordinate vendors and any testing window.
2025-01-11 Ethan Brooks: Assigned to me. I'll do a quick feasibility check on off-the-shelf temp sensors and a weight-sensor approach. ETA: initial options by 2025-01-15.
2025-01-14 Aisha Patel (People Ops): Thanks Ethan — we can provide access to power/network near the kitchen. For inventory, a simple weekly snapshot is fine for MVP.

2025-01-15 Ethan Brooks: Feasibility note attached in comments: off-the-shelf wifi temp sensors look good for temperature logging and alerting; weight sensors are finicky for variable containers, camera+OCR/RFID seems more robust for inventory but higher effort. Proposing temp-monitoring pilot first, inventory as Phase 2. Planning to order 2 sensors and test in next week.
